LESSON: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING – GRADE- APPROPRIATE TEXTS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts, part of Strand 9 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we read for information? 2. How can we ensure we live harmoniously with all the other Kenyan communities?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read grade-appropriate texts and outline the main ideas,

2. identify vocabulary from the texts,

3. work with peers to find the meaning of the new words from context,

4. play a language game to match the vocabulary identified to their synonyms,

5. identify prepositions used from the texts read and create a list,

6. use the vocabulary identified and prepositions to construct sentences related to the theme,

7. write a summary of the key ideas in the texts read,

8. create a reading log with details of grade-appropriate texts read (e.g. title, author, characters, setting, summary of events, vocabulary),

9. team up with peers to prepare a mosaic on a creative idea presenting Kenyan cultures. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read grade-appropriate texts and outline the main ideas,
2. identify vocabulary from the texts,
3. work with peers to find the meaning of the new words from context,
4. play a language game to match the vocabulary identified to their synonyms,
5. identify prepositions used from the texts read and create a list,
6. use the vocabulary identified and prepositions to construct sentences related to the theme,
7. write a summary of the key ideas in the texts read,
8. create a reading log with details of grade-appropriate texts read (e.g. title, author, characters, setting, summary of events, vocabulary),
9. team up with peers to prepare a mosaic on a creative idea presenting Kenyan cultures. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: The learner is motivated to learn continuously by using the vocabulary identified to construct

sentences related to the theme.

• Critical Thinking and Problem-solving: The learner follows simple instructions when playing a language game to match

the vocabulary identified to their synonyms.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner diligently creates a reading log with details of grade-appropriate texts read.

• Unity: It is promoted as the learner works with peers to find the meaning of the new words from context.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Human Rights: This is promoted as the learner experiences a sense of association with other cultures.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of interaction with other Kenyan cultures to the concept of living together in Religious

Studies.
